itens.texto: The channel list no longer shows feeds and direct conversations that wait for a seat as "Your channel, joining the channel". They still ask for their seats, and a community that waits for one still shows as joining.

A crash in the app shell no longer leaves a black screen. The whole app now sits behind the crash card: "Error 901", Reload and Report a bug. The sync state is in the vault, so a reload resumes the sync.

Crashes, uncaught errors and unhandled promise rejections go to the diagnostic log with the version, a short stack and whether a sync was running. Addresses, links and message text are stripped. A crash survives the reload, so the log after Reload still has it.
History between devices: a media response larger than the responder's 16 MiB buffer (a 25 MiB video) is now windowed and kept, so a lost part can be asked again instead of failing forever.

History between devices: a media item that fails 3 times (the sender cannot serve it, or goes silent while still online) is skipped, so the sync ends. Reloads, sleep and a closed sender do not count. The progress bar reaches the end and says how many files did not come.

History between devices: a page that never arrives (an older sender that cannot send it, or no longer keeps it) is asked at most 3 times. The rest of that channel then counts as not received and leaves the total, so the sync goes on with the other channels. The bar says how many messages did not come.

Lock on its own no longer stops the history between devices: it waits while the history really moves (a part in the last 2 min) on a visible page, for at most 60 min per sync. A stopped sync or a hidden page locks as before, Lock now always locks, and the unlock screen says "Locked. The history continues after you unlock."

Own profile: a device that came in by the account file now takes a newer profile from your other devices in any channel, live or in history, not only in the account channel, and publishes it again. An older local edit still waiting to go out loses; a portrait whose bytes did not come keeps the one on this device.
"You have not saved the account file yet" no longer shows on a device that came in by the file, and never shows in the phone layout. Export stays in Settings.
Common room: a device that can no longer read it (Error 390) now takes the room's join card and seats itself again, with no other member online.
Seat requests from a new device (import or pairing) now run on their own timer, at 1, 2, 4 and up to 30 min, instead of waiting for the next 10-minute pass.
A device waiting for a seat asks again as soon as a member of that channel comes online. That member first finishes its own catch-up (up to 30 s), then answers.
A channel whose group state was lost on this device (history, but no group) now asks for its seat, signed, like a new device does.

Common room join card: when a card is taken and the join never lands, the server tells the seated members and one of them posts the card again, at most once a minute. A newcomer can no longer be left waiting for a member to let them in.
Key packages: after wasting 3 of another device's packages in 30 minutes, a session stops claiming that device until the window ends, so a run of refused commits can no longer drain a device to zero.
Sidebar: a channel waiting for this device's seat shows with its name and "joining the channel" until it opens, instead of being missing from the list.

History for new members: someone who joins a channel late now reads what was said before they joined. Another member's device sends it, end to end encrypted, and rooms in a category restricted to roles they don't hold stay out.
While that history is arriving, the conversation says "Chat history is syncing." When there is nothing to bring, it says nothing.
Polls made before you joined reach you as polls, with their close and the votes already cast.

Phone layout: below 841 px the app has four tabs at the bottom (Communities, Messages, Friends, You). A conversation opens full screen, and the back arrow, the browser back button or a swipe from the left edge goes back. Context menus open as a sheet with the same entries.

Anti-abuse for open servers: a proof of work when an account is created, a cap on new accounts per network, a slower pace for new accounts in the common room (3 messages, then 1 every 30 s on the first day and every 10 s up to 72 h), plain links and hidden attachments from new authors there, and a join queue. A live invite link from an established community still gets a new account past the network cap.
Nudges shake and play on every device of both accounts.

Import the account file as a new device: the import adds a device and never removes one. The other devices show "A new device joined the account." with a Remove button, and a failed import retries with the same device key, so it never takes a second seat.

New sign-in and sign-up screens, with three ways in: create an account, the account file, another device. One account password on every device: a new device asks for it after the words, and Settings › Account and security › Change the password changes it everywhere (or with I forgot the current password, proven by the open vault, and by Touch ID on macOS).

Channel cap: an account creates 1 channel in its first 72 h, and holds at most 5 at a time (a channel everyone left frees its place). At the cap the + stays, greyed out, and says why on hover, on keyboard focus and on a tap; the server refuses with Error 368. Join with a link still works.

Room cap: an account creates up to 12 rooms in its first 72 h, and holds at most 30 (deleting a room frees its place, and the rooms a channel starts with don't count). At the cap New room and the category + stay, greyed out, and say why the same way; the server refuses with Error 369.
Invite links past the network limit: all the invites one account makes let in at most one network's worth of new accounts (3 an hour, 10 a day).
Pair a new device with a 6-character code (CPace, one try per code, expires in 5 minutes); the QR and the long code still work.

History on join brings the newest 100 lines of each room instead of everything. Load older goes back 100 lines at a time: past what this device holds, it asks a member online for the next page, and says Error 395 when no member online has it.
The members column goes grey while a channel's history syncs, with "Now syncing" at the top and, on a device that has been here before, "You have not signed in for X days".

Fast server start: about a second on a large database instead of 87 s, with a timing line per startup phase in the log. The reverse proxy waits for the server while it restarts instead of answering 502.
The member count leaves out accounts the server's roster says are gone, and a departure the server agrees with is swept from the channel.
Profile bios are 300 characters (an emoji counts as one), with a counter near the end. Longer bios from older clients still load, cut at 300.
Channel list: both + buttons sit at the right end of their line, where the unread counts end, with 44 px touch targets.
Server messages are in English first, including the registration and media refusals.

Profiles go out in their latest version only: an edit is published 5 s after the last change, so edits in a row are one version, and a newcomer pulls each member's latest signed profile instead of every member resending theirs. A pending edit goes out before lock or quit, within 2 s, or on the next opening.
After sign-in, the loading screen stays until the app is online and 2 s more (10 s at most), so the layout no longer opens while still connecting.
macOS: the Bluetooth permission prompt now says Orwell does not use Bluetooth, that Bluetooth headphones work without it, and that Don't Allow is safe.
The "How it works" link is gone from the sign-in screen.
The "How to reach someone" card is gone from the first screen after sign-up. Join with a link, adding a friend and your address are where they were: the channel list, Friends and Settings.

macOS: the microphone works on Intel Macs. The whole universal app, both the arm64 and x86_64 slices and every helper, is signed ad hoc, so macOS asks for the microphone instead of handing the call silence. On Apple silicon the permission dialog comes up once and the answer is kept. A refused microphone or camera now says so and opens the Privacy panel.

Seat repair: a device signs its own seat request, so a server can no longer push a live device out of a channel. A device with no keys left is claimed once, and a member coming online brings forward the seat request of a room that went deaf.
iPhone and the installed web app: locking the screen or switching apps no longer reloads Orwell. It resumes where it was.
Key packages no longer run out when several members repair the same seat at once: a package a lost epoch left unspent is kept and used for the next repair.

History between devices travels in windows and survives a dropped connection: the parts that already came stay, and the next connection asks only for what is missing. The stopped notice no longer sticks, and its number counts the messages really missing on this device.
Joining the common room from its card now records where you joined, so the history count starts at the right place.
Incoming call ring stops when you answer on another device; Decline silences it on this device.
Poll votes synced to late joiners are filtered by room permissions.
YouTube links pasted and sent at once now carry their thumbnail; link previews are matched to their request.
Desktop: the app quits after SIGTERM. The second quit ran in the same task as the first and was cleared, leaving a windowless process on macOS; it now quits in under 1 s.
Call card: the "⋯" menu and the voice wave no longer overlap. The wave sits in the name's row and the menu has its own 44 px corner.

"Catching up on this conversation…" sits under the message box on a line that is always reserved, so the conversation no longer jumps. It shows only after 400 ms of catch-up and stays at least 1.5 s, so it no longer blinks.

The opening's fade can no longer stay on top of the app when the tab freezes: the hold now ends by itself in CSS 3 s after the opening leaves, the fade carries no background, and a tab that comes back cleans up at once.
One call per account: joining a call on another device takes the call there, and the first device leaves it with a notice instead of reconnecting.
Server admins choose who may create an account: open, invite only or closed (ENCLAVE_REGISTO). Existing accounts and their new devices always get in.
English is the default language. The app opens in Portuguese when the system's first language is Portuguese, and your own choice always wins.
Animated GIFs: up to 2 MiB in messages and 1 MiB in posts, sent intact and still moving. The desktop app makes their thumbnails too.
Shift+Enter starts a new line, and the message box grows up to half the conversation. On a phone, Enter starts a new line and the button sends.
Pinned messages: the newest pin shows on a bar at the top of the room, and a pinned message stays in the vault however old it gets.
Formatting from the message box: Cmd/Ctrl+E for code, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H for hidden text (it was Shift+E, the screen share key), undo works after a formatting key, and a bar over selected text.
Blocking reaches shared rooms: a blocked person's messages fold into one line with Show, ring nothing, count nowhere, and their reactions leave the counts.
A nudge is heard anywhere in the app and shows on the Friends button until you open Friends or the conversation.
Privacy Policy and Terms links when you create an account on orwell.pt, and in Settings › Help.
A + next to a category's name creates a room in it.
A device that falls behind in a room now tells you, holds your messages until it catches up, and asks for its place again.

Rail badges have a shape each: a pill for unread, a number for what waits for you, a glyph for a nudge, a green seal for a call, an amber seal when the connection drops. The Communities number counts mentions only.

Self-hosting: the encrypted vault of a channel that nobody is subscribed to any more is erased after 90 days by default (ENCLAVE_COFRE_GC_DIAS, 0 turns it off), and the compose file bounds container logs.
Load older loads whole lines of the conversation, keeps what it loaded and leaves you on the line you were reading.
Invite and friend links open inside the app instead of the browser.
Desktop app: room permissions work, so "Who can write", roles and read-only rooms behave as on the web.
A device asking for its place in a room no longer pushes your other devices out, even when they are offline.
Keys refill when they run out, so a seat that failed for lack of keys can be given again.
The "Receiving the channel" bar no longer sticks.
A quick reply no longer shows above the message it answers.
Reaction counts on older messages include every reaction this device has stored, not only the ones in memory.
The conversation stays at the bottom when the reply bar or a taller message box opens under it.
The "You joined here" marker no longer lands below the messages you sent right after joining.
Pinned images get their thumbnail again, and an image left without one asks again on the next opening.
Polls that showed as plain text because this device did not yet know their author's role come back as polls once the role arrives.
A poll that closes during the session stays in the Closed tab.
The polls room and the polls page show every poll again, not only the recent ones; an open poll stays in place however many messages come after it.
A deleted poll leaves a line saying it was deleted by its author or by moderation.
The small avatar in a reply's quote no longer grows to full size over the message.

nota: Optional Windows updates suggested by Kafein

itens.texto: Creating polls is a role power: "create polls". The founder and admins always have it; give it to another role in the channel settings.
Delete a poll: its author or someone who moderates. Its votes go with it.
Windows: choose whether updates install automatically or ask first, in Settings › Account. A new version must be public on GitHub, and this device waits up to 72 hours before it installs it.

nota: Light theme and flat redesign by edtimer · gate name limit found by viniciussilva2504

itens.texto: Themes: Dark (the default), Light, System and Aurora, the previous look. Choose one in Settings › Account.
Reactions work like on Discord: one per person per message. Another emoji switches yours; the same emoji takes it back.
"@" and "#" link to rooms in a message.
The app is faster when you switch channels, open menus and scroll.
Long conversations keep their old messages. What no longer fits on the device goes to an encrypted archive, and "Load older" reads it.
Only accounts 5 days old or more can vote in polls.
The name at signup has 12 characters at most, the same rule as the display name.
A new device always gets every channel, also when its first invite does not open.
A device with many channels gets all of them and their live messages; no channel is left silent after many subscriptions.
Poll votes no longer reset.
Mention highlights fade once seen.
The unread bar goes away after reading.
Display names are up to 12 characters.
In the member list, status sits on a second line after the role.
Messages that arrived while a long catch-up was paused are no longer skipped.
The "+X people on this server" list no longer stacks its rows.
Mention highlights keep their background on hover and after a tap, and no longer flash.
The emoji picker uses our own emoji font, so flags and newer emoji show on Windows, and its card is opaque.
Live messages and unread counters arrive while the Safari window is covered or in the background.
"is typing" sits above the message box and no longer moves the conversation.
The polls room is a normal room: you can drag, rename and delete it, and deleting it deletes its polls.

Reactions on messages, in channels and direct messages: hover a message and press React, or long-press on a phone. Chips under the message show each emoji with its count; tap one to add or remove yours. Reactions travel inside the encrypted message, and the server never sees the target or the emoji.

Room and role tags in the message box: # suggests the rooms you can see, @ suggests people, then roles, then @all. Mentioning a role or @all needs the "mention everyone and roles" permission, unless the role allows anyone to mention it. A role mention notifies its members like a direct mention, and a message that mentions you is highlighted.

Read-only rooms: a room can let only some roles write. Admins set it from the room menu ("Who can write") or when creating the room. Everyone else sees a line in place of the message box, and the other members' apps drop messages from people without the permission. When someone gives you a role, you get one notice, only for a recent assignment and only if your roles changed.

Screen sharing is now a role permission (transmitir). Without it, the button is greyed out with a hint. The person sharing sees a thumbnail with Stop instead of their own screen on stage; viewers see who is in the call over the shared screen. Voice rooms in the sidebar show mic off, sound off and muted-by-me marks.

Pinned messages stay pinned until someone unpins or deletes them, for people who join later, new devices and members who were away longer than the retention period. Pins keep file names and a small thumbnail of the first image. The server's event numbering no longer restarts at 0 when retention empties a channel.

Report a bug, in Settings > Help and diagnostics and on the error screen. The form shows exactly what is sent (app version, platform, browser, language, the last 20 error codes and connection state) and what is never sent. Contact details are only kept if you tick the box.

Save your account file: right after creating an account, a step asks you to download the account file (.enclave), locked with your password, and to confirm you kept it somewhere safe. On an iPhone, Share opens the share sheet (Save to Files). An account that already exists sees a one-time notice with the same button. An account kept in the system keychain asks for a password for the file first.
The emoji picker has the full Unicode 15.0 list, generated from CLDR 42 data kept in the repo. The catalog loads on first open, out of the main bundle.

The official Orwell channel is opt-in: registration asks with an unticked box, and you can join later from the join dialog. Leaving it works like any other channel, and the app no longer puts you back.
The interface opens in English until you choose another language in Settings. The browser and system language no longer decide. ?lingua= in the address still works.

Opening a direct message with someone who is not your friend no longer notifies them, and an empty DM no longer shows in their list. The buzz has its own icon and button, only in DMs, and with reduced motion it still shakes, slower and shorter, instead of flashing blue.

The "edited" mark sits on its own line under the message, with the edit time on hover or tap. A day separator appears before the first message of each local day. The unread bar only shows when the unread mark is above the view, and leaves once seen. On wide screens the history progress sits in the channel's top bar.

Large channels: with more than 50 members the member panel lists who is online and a "+X people" row that opens the full, windowed list. On joining the common room only the names of online members are requested; the rest are requested when needed.

Notifications show names by default and never the room identifier; with content hidden they say "You have a new message". Mentions and DMs notify and play a sound only when they arrive live, once per message, not again when history catches up.

Images and files on demand: the request goes to the author first, then only to members the server reports as online. A "don't have it" reply no longer ends the request, and when nobody online has the file the message says so.
Phone parity: a paired phone with the main device off asks channel members for the seats it lacks, and seating retries after 5 minutes instead of 6 hours. The profile bio fits on narrow screens.

History catch-up: above the server's page cap the server now answers with retryAfterMs instead of silence, pages hold 200 events, and a long catch-up continues on the same connection. The server serializes each broadcast once for all connections.

Signal rate limits: the allowance for light senders in a busy channel is counted per account, not per connection. A nameless account that no relay answered for is asked again after 10 minutes instead of 24 hours.

Notifications when the app is closed (Web Push), in Settings › Notifications, under "System notifications". The server sends an empty, encrypted push to the devices that have no connection open, and the phone shows "New message in Orwell", with no name and no text. At most one per device every 2 minutes; muted channels, Busy and paused notifications are respected. On an iPhone it needs the app on the Home Screen (iOS 16.4 or later). Server operators: off unless ENCLAVE_PUSH=on, and the switch only shows on a server that turns it on.

Calls in the background: the lock screen and the system media controls show the room, with mute and hang up wired to the same actions as the call buttons. Safari keeps a play-and-record audio session during the call. A new option in Settings › Microphone and camera keeps the screen on during calls (off by default).

Unlocking the phone in a call: the microphone is checked when the page comes back, and a muted or ended track is reopened at once instead of the watchdog giving up in the background. The connection is checked within 5 seconds, time without a connection no longer counts against rebuilding the call, and a call keeps the tab when the browser puts the page in its back/forward cache, so coming back no longer reloads it.

On the iPhone's installed app, joining a call shows a notice: iOS turns off the microphone of installed web apps when the screen locks, and it comes back on unlock. To talk with the screen locked, use Safari.
The server closes a connection that misses two control pings (60 to 90 seconds), so a phone that went to sleep leaves the call instead of staying in it as a silent participant.

Returning to a minimized window is lighter: while you read at the bottom, the conversation keeps a sliding window of lines instead of piling up every message that arrived while hidden; incoming messages render as a transition, so your first click draws first; the audio context starts after the first frame of the gesture; media blobs decrypt in a Worker (web) or a worker thread (desktop); and the batched vault write exports groups one at a time.

Settings › Devices has "Space for images and files on this device": pick a ceiling (250 MB to 2 GB, or none), see what is in use, and "Free up space". An image that left this device keeps its sharp thumbnail and a "Fetch" button, which asks your other devices first and then the members.
Exporting the account can include the images. Off by default: the file stays the vault alone. Importing reads both kinds of file, and says how many images did not fit.

Images and files no longer live inside the vault. Each device keeps them in its own encrypted media store, and the vault keeps only references and keys. On a loaded account the vault went from 7.4 MB to 2.8 MB and the longest save from 287 ms to 96 ms. An older vault moves its media on the first unlock, one piece at a time, and a crash halfway loses nothing. What goes on the wire is unchanged, so older versions keep reading it.

Typing lag on large accounts: every key redrew the whole app (the sidebar, the member list and the conversation). The draft now lives in the composer and only goes up when you switch channel or send, so drafts still survive a channel switch. @ suggestions no longer refold every name on each key.
The first click created 28 audio contexts at once, about 60 MB. Sounds now share one context, and each sound is built the first time it plays.

Coming back after the app was minimized: the sync clock that fires late now joins the catch-up already running instead of starting a second full pass, and the catch-up yields between channels. The diagnostic log records each return (time the page was held, vault saves, late timers, how long the desktop main process was held, whether the connection dropped), with no message content.
The diagnostic log endpoint now requires a signed request from a signed-in session, like the report routes. An anonymous request is refused.
Direct calls no longer fall back to a third-party STUN server. If the homeserver offers no STUN or TURN, the call says so with Erro 493 instead of leaking your address to an outside service.
Dependencies updated (fastify, zod, fast-uri, Electron). `npm audit` reports no vulnerabilities in production dependencies.
CI on GitHub: every push and pull request installs, typechecks, runs the test suites and audits the production dependencies.

Login freeze on large accounts: when the profile repair round failed in one channel, every login sent the profile again to every channel. The round now tracks each channel, so a failing channel is retried alone, and an unchanged profile is not sent at all.

An admin who logs in after someone joined the public community by the invite card no longer sends the community state during login. It waits until the app is idle, goes out in small pieces, and is skipped if another admin already sent it. The newcomer still gets it.

Less memory and CPU when the local vault is saved. A save now builds the encrypted file in one buffer, instead of holding five to eleven copies of the vault at once. The file on disk is byte for byte the same.

Fewer vault saves at startup: the profile goes to all channels at once, and sends that leave in the same moment share one save. On a loaded account the profile publish went from two saves per channel to one or two in total.

Mobile restarts and the desktop freeze after login: every admin device re-sent the whole state of every channel it runs (roles, every role assignment, rooms, categories, banner) on every connection and on every join. In a large community that was ~176 messages per connection, each one a full write of the local vault on the sender and a decrypt, write and render on every member. Channel state is no longer re-sent on connect. On a join it is sent once: by the inviter, or in the public community by one admin, taking turns. Anything still missing arrives by sync from one member.

Bursts from older versions are now cheap to receive: a role, assignment, room, category or banner identical to what the device already has is dropped on arrival, and live messages enter the list in one render per frame instead of one per message.
Startup writes the local vault once after catching up all channels, instead of once per channel.

Mobile crash loop after "Sync the account": the button clears the list of invites that can no longer be opened, and on the next start the server sends all of them again (up to 200). Each one that failed wrote the whole local vault at once, in parallel, and a phone browser ran out of memory before any write finished, so the page crashed at every start ("A problem repeatedly occurred" on iOS). Those invites are now marked in one write, and the vault never runs two full writes at the same time: writes that arrive during one share the next. An account in this state recovers on its own at the next start, and no data is deleted.

History from the main device no longer stands still: an entry that cannot be sent is skipped and counted instead of failing the whole page, lost entries leave the total, and with no progress for 3 minutes the notice closes with the reason and the transfer retries quietly every 5 minutes.
The catch-up notice in a conversation now only says "Catching up on this conversation…". Messages typed meanwhile still wait for the catch-up.

Faster startup: the app opens as soon as the vault is unlocked, and catch-up runs four channels at once, starting with the channels you used last. On a throttled phone with a busy common room, time to a usable screen went from 30.9 s to 1.3 s.

Faster startup in large rooms: catching up on history saves the local vault once per room (and at most every 10 s) instead of once per page of 100 events. The server now allows 300 history pages per minute per account instead of 60.

Joining the common room no longer makes every online member republish their profile and the room's join card. The member who made the commit publishes the card once per epoch, and named members only republish when no relay carried their profile.
Typing indicators are sent as ephemeral encrypted signals and are no longer stored on the server. With more than 3 people typing, the line says "Several people are typing…".

Connection check: liveness now counts any frame from the server, not only the pong. A check waits up to 15 s and only reconnects when nothing at all arrives, so a slow pong no longer drops a working connection. Sending never waits for a check. The 25 s check while the page is visible only asks after 60 s of silence. In 1.3.6 a pong later than 5 s closed the socket, which doubled reconnects and caused message delays and dropped calls.

Mobile sync: when the page comes back after 30 s or more with no frame received, on a touch device or a frozen page, the app reconnects at once instead of waiting for a ping. The new connection fetches every channel from where it stopped, commits included and in order. Messages typed right after coming back wait for that channel's catch-up (up to 10 s), so they are encrypted on the current epoch.

Messages sent into a connection that turned out to be dead are sent again after the reconnect, on the current epoch. Before, they showed as sent and never arrived. If the server did get the first copy, other devices still show the message once.

Calls: when the connection drops during a call, the app rejoins the call up to 3 times within 30 s and shows "The call is connecting again" meanwhile. Error 403 only appears if all tries fail. Before, one failed rejoin ended the call.

Images and files on request: an online member whose device has the bytes is asked even if that device has not spoken in the channel since you reloaded. A real failure now shows Error 515 instead of "no member with this image is connected".

Second devices: coming back to the page also runs the sync pass (at most once a minute) and asks the other devices of the account for history again. A device outside the account channel announces itself on the periodic pass too, and a device with no key packages is retried after 10 minutes instead of 6 hours.

Language: a browser or system set only to languages Orwell does not have (German, French, Spanish and so on) now gets English instead of Portuguese. A ?lingua= link and a saved choice still win, and pt or en anywhere in the system list is still used.
Desktop app: choosing "Automatic" in Settings > Account > Language follows the operating system's languages again, the same list the app uses at startup.

Mobile sync: when the page comes back (tab switch, unlock, network change, back-forward cache) and every 25 s while it is visible, the app pings the server with a 5 s timeout. A dead connection is closed and reopened at once, missed messages are fetched, and messages written meanwhile wait and go out after the reconnect. Before, the status could say "connected" over a dead socket and messages went nowhere.
Mobile: the side rail scrolls on short landscape screens, so Settings is always reachable (iPhone SE and iPhone 13 in landscape).
Mobile: Settings opens with its list of sections. Tap one to open it, and the back button returns to the list. Before, the sections were only in the side drawer.
Mobile: all four Friends tabs fit on screen. "Find" is no longer cut off.
Mobile: the message box is wider. The Send button shows an icon instead of the word, and the touch targets stay at 44 px.
Mobile: the direct message header stays on one line, with icon-only call, video and search buttons.
The "request sent" notice goes away when you open the direct message or when the request gets an answer. It no longer covers the message box.
The Windows installer is always in English, whatever the system language, with no language picker.
The Windows installer's finish page links to Ko-fi (https://ko-fi.com/orwell_eu) to support the project.
The macOS disk image has a "Support Orwell" link to Ko-fi next to the drag-to-Applications window.
The Windows .exe file description and the macOS system-audio permission prompt (screen sharing with sound) are now in English.

Desktop downloads go from 1.3.3 straight to 1.3.5, so desktop users also get everything in 1.3.4: Orwell is open source under the AGPL-3.0, with a "Source code" link in Settings > Help and diagnostics.
Orwell is now open source under the AGPL-3.0: https://github.com/magnuslab-sudo/orwell. A "Source code" link sits in Settings > Help and diagnostics and in the site footer.
The web app serves its source maps again.

Shared room: an account that rejoins through the room card from another device (browser to desktop app, for example) now stays in the channel and gets the echo of its own commit. Before, the commit was taken as lost after 10 s and retried once a minute, bumping the room epoch every time.
Desktop installers ship the licence (LICENSE), the copyright notice (NOTICE) and the third-party notices next to the program.
orwell.pt: support now goes through Ko-fi only (https://ko-fi.com/orwell_eu), with a "Support us" link next to Sign in and the Support link in the footer.

Replies. You can now reply to a specific message, like on Discord: the reply arrow in the hover bar, "Reply" in the context menu (long-press on mobile), R on a focused message, or swipe left on touch. A "Replying to {name}" bar sits above the composer with an "@ Mention" toggle (on by default; pings the original author through the normal mention path) and an X. Esc cancels, and a pending reply sticks to its room like a draft.

Replies show a one-line quote of the original (avatar, name, start of the text, "Image" or the file name). Clicking it jumps to the original and highlights it, pulling older history from the vault when needed. Deleted originals and originals this device never had say so instead of guessing.

Wire format unchanged: replies use the existing encrypted replyTo field, so 1.1.x to 1.3.2 clients see them as plain messages, and the server learns nothing new. Ticket rooms keep their own reply flow. Desktop and web now build the outgoing message with the same function.
Under reduced motion, the jump highlight (replies and search) now fades slower instead of snapping off.

SFU calls: a consume refused by the server is no longer final when the refusal can be a timing issue (app frozen for a few seconds, the other side rebuilding its media). Before, the person stayed silent until you left and rejoined. Only refusals that cannot change by waiting are final (incompatible codec, no seat, server full, wrong transport direction, no SFU, call caps). The rest retry at 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 s, then wait for a signal: the person's voice.join or a new producer, an epoch change, or the receive transport reconnecting.

SFU calls: the client resyncs with the server's producer list (a repeated sfu.scope.join, no protocol change) after an "unknown" refusal, after a long main-thread stall, and after a slow sfu.consume reply. Dead producers are dropped, consumers whose producer.closed was lost are closed, and producers whose producer.new was lost are consumed. Two unknown-transport refusals in a row rebuild the call media.

Someone whose voice is still missing is no longer shown as "connected". The card says "in the call, no sound yet", with notice 453 ("You cannot hear {name} yet. The app is asking for the sound again."). Every refusal is logged with the server's code. Media still never flows without SFrame.

SFU calls no longer drop you with Error 448 the first time the media encryption is not ready. The sender retries the whole SFrame setup (key, worker ACK, transform) at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 8 s, and right away on every epoch change; when it succeeds the source goes live by itself. Nothing is sent unencrypted while it waits. Meanwhile the call stays up (you still hear everyone) and shows notice 449 ("Your microphone is not sending yet: preparing the encryption."). Error 448 only shows after the last attempt. Same for camera, screen, screen audio and music. Receivers without decryption now also retry on a timer, not only on the next commit.

A microphone that dies silently mid-call now comes back by itself. The app watches the capture track (ended, muted for 3 s), the audio context (not running for 2 s) and the voice chain worklet (processorerror, or no heartbeat for 3 s), reopens the same input device with the same processing and swaps the track into the same encrypted sender (replaceTrack), without leaving the call. If the mic keeps dying (more than 4 times a minute), the app stops and shows Error 452.
One NaN or Infinity in the voice chain (noise suppressor included) no longer silences your mic until you rejoin. The chain resets its state and drops one block instead.
An SFU send transport that never connects (or fails mid-call) is now logged and the call media is rebuilt automatically, up to 3 times a minute, keeping your capture.

Role order is now editable where you manage roles. The founder and admins can drag a role or use the Move up / Move down buttons (keyboard and screen-reader friendly, with a live announcement of the new position). The order is the signed rank, so every client shows the same order: member list groups, the role line under each name, profiles and role menus. Admin stays pinned on top. Delegated role managers can't reorder. New roles start at the bottom, for 1.1.x clients too. Desktop: added the reorder IPC; the app had no way to reorder before.

Settings > Notifications > Sounds: turning a sound type on now plays it, the way the master "Sounds" switch already plays the direct-message sound. Before, enabling any of the 27 per-type toggles was silent, so it looked like nothing had been enabled. Disabling stays silent. All 27 types are now covered end to end through the real sound engine with pre-1.2 stored preferences, and in real Chromium with an analyser on the output.

Chat: opening a room no longer scrolls on its own. Switching rooms inside the same channel was treated as "new messages arrived", so the timeline smooth-scrolled from the top to the bottom or, coming from a bigger room, didn't scroll at all. Scroll state is now keyed on channel + room, each room restores its own position, and returns to the bottom if you left it there.

Chat: images and YouTube thumbnails reserve their final box before decoding. Image dimensions are read from the data: URL header (PNG, GIF, WebP, JPEG incl. EXIF orientation); YouTube cards get a fixed 480px width. Rooms used to open 400-1500px above the bottom once images finished decoding. Following new messages at the bottom is now instant and happens before paint; only scrolling up detaches you from the bottom, and an image finishing loading keeps you pinned.

Chat: removed the horizontal scrollbar above the composer (always visible on Windows). The hidden tooltip of the rightmost message action overflowed the timeline by ~53px; it now opens towards the inside.

Fixed freezes after someone joins a big channel (calls cutting out, the app hanging for seconds). The vault was rewritten in full for every live event; it is now written at most once a second for live application messages, while commits, Welcomes, catch-up, sends and flush still write at once. One join in a 120-member room went from 116 vault writes to 9; in Chromium at 4x CPU slowdown with a 10.7 MB vault, main-thread busy time per join dropped from 35-41 s to 4.4 s and the longest task from 5.1-13.4 s to 0.64-0.68 s. A crash loses at most the last second of events, which the server sends again.

Channel admins no longer stall after each join. Every send writes the whole vault before the frame leaves (so the ratchet never reuses a generation after a crash), and the cascade an admin sends to each newcomer (one role.assign per role holder, categories, rooms) was ~100 sends: 101 full vault writes and ~6 s of CPU per join with a 13 MB vault, holding the group while the next commit and the media key waited. The cascade is now encrypted in one go, the vault is written once after the last message, and the frames go out in the same order: 8-9 writes per join, and the room settles in 5-6 s instead of 13-14 s.

Web: every vault write ran a JS FNV hash twice over the whole file, on the page thread inside the IndexedDB transaction (18 s of 54 s of writes with an 11 MB vault at 4x CPU slowdown). The tab-ownership stamp now hashes 4 KB from each end plus the size. Old full-hash stamps still verify, so updating mid-session keeps ownership.

Checkboxes: the check glyph is now centred in its box at every display scale. It was an 11px clip-path box sitting 1/3px low and pixel-snapped on its own, so at 125% and 150% it drifted up to 1.5 device px (most visible on "Remember session" at sign-in on Windows). The ::before now fills the box and draws the check as a centred mask. Measured in Chromium and Electron at 1x, 1.25x and 1.5x.

Members without a display name (or whose profile hasn't reached you yet) now show the first word of their address, capitalised, instead of "No name": @ginvodra-sastybis-…:orwell.pt reads as Ginvodra. Address-derived names are rendered in italics in the secondary colour with a "From the address" title, so they can't pass for a chosen name. Two unnamed accounts on the same screen sharing a first word both get their second word too. Applies everywhere a name is shown, federated addresses included.

Reworked the report window. Three steps (Reason, Review, Send) with a step indicator. The reason step shows the reported message or person on top, with the note, good-faith box and contact under the reasons. Review shows the reported message with a red bar, the context in dimmer cards, a summary of everything that leaves the device, and the long addresses behind "Show addresses". On phones it is a bottom sheet with the button pinned above the safe area. Fixes the time running into names and badges, addresses breaking lines and list numbers over the text.

Reports inbox (Channel properties > Moderation) now has the app's look: one card per report with the reason, day, reported person, channel, room and a "Verified" / "Not verified" proof badge, the note, and the messages with the reported one marked.

Founder copies now reach every device of the founder's account. The device with the account key opens the copy and passes it, already open, to your other devices over the encrypted account channel. A paired device shows "N reports are waiting" until then, instead of "Nobody reported anything". The server learns nothing new. Both devices need this version.

Reports: message menu or member menu > "Report…". Eight reasons, an optional note and contact, and a preview of exactly what leaves the device before you send. Reported messages carry the author's autoria signature, so the server and the channel founder can verify who wrote them. Attachments go as name, type and size only, never the file.

Founder copy: when the report comes from a channel and the founder is in it, the founder gets a sealed copy in Channel properties > Moderation, 1 to 6 hours later. No reporter address, no reporter messages, and only the day of the report.

Account suspension (server): an operator can suspend an account until a set day or until review. The gateway and key package endpoints refuse it. Nothing is automatic and no report count suspends anyone. The suspended account sees the full notice (measure, duration, scope, facts, rule, redress) and can ask for a review.
The reporter gets the decision ("account suspended" or "no action") in the notification bell.
Terms and privacy: new Reports section, a single contact address (orwell.eu@proton.me), and the review deadline set to 30 days.

Security: SFU calls no longer publish media that is not end-to-end encrypted. The SFrame transform is attached before the sender is negotiated (mediasoup onRtpSender), and the media key (plus the worker ACK on Firefox and Safari) must be ready before a producer is created. If encryption cannot be set up, the producer is closed locally and on the server before any RTP goes out: for the mic you leave the call; for camera, screen, screen audio and music only that source is dropped. Error 448 says which. Reported by an external audit of 1.1.0 (SEC-02).
Security: SFU calls no longer play a stream whose decryption could not be installed. It stays paused on the server instead of reaching the decoder.

Security: when someone is removed from the channel's MLS group mid-call, their media keys are wiped in both decryptors (main thread and worker, with ACK), and their streams are paused on the server and dropped from what you hear and see, whatever their roster presence. People re-seated on a new MLS leaf keep being heard. Reported by an external audit of 1.1.0 (SEC-03).

Security (server): one account per socket. The gateway refuses auth.begin and auth.finish on a socket that is already signed in (already-authenticated, fatal). A second login on the same socket used to inherit the first account's channel set (AUTH-02).

Security (server): redeeming an invite no longer grants a seat. invite.redeem only forwards invite.request to connected members; the seat comes from the directed Welcome. channel.groupinfo.take grants a 2-minute temporary seat that accepts exactly one external commit for that channel, and becomes a subscription only when that commit is accepted as the epoch's commit (INV-01).

Security (server): redemption ceilings. Key packages are capped at 8 KiB, invite.redeem checks the MLS key_package header before spending a use, and redemptions are rate limited per account, invite, channel and server (invite.rejected rate-limited, no use spent). Repeated pending requests are not broadcast again, and a connection with more than 64 MiB queued is terminated (INV-02).

Security (server): federation verifies the signature before spending the nonce, so a bad signature writes nothing. Nonces must be base64url, 16 to 64 chars, with per-origin ceilings on envelopes, key package claims and key-directory fetches. Federation is still off by default (FED-01).
An invite refused for too many requests now shows Error 365 ("Too many invite requests. Wait one minute and try again."). Older clients show "That invite no longer exists." in that case.
Licence: Orwell is now proprietary software (all rights reserved); third-party notices ship with the app and the site (/terceiros.txt). The web build no longer publishes source maps.

Security (server): the server now sees each client's real IP behind the reverse proxy, so per-IP limits (diagnostic reports) apply per person and not to the whole server. Forwarded-for headers sent by clients are ignored (NET-01). Missing files under /app/assets/ now answer 404 instead of the app page.

Call sounds for the moments Discord marks: outgoing ring while you wait for a DM call to be answered, voice connection lost, moved to another room by a moderator, stream started and ended, and someone starting or stopping watching your stream. All synthesized in Orwell's own sound family. Each one has its own toggle in Settings > Notifications > Sounds.

New sound set with a mallet (marimba) timbre and a short room echo. Message, mention, friend online, ringing and nudge have new figures. The update sound has a new figure, so it no longer sounds like friend online.
Being moved to another voice room no longer also plays your own join and the "connected" sound.
Startup animation no longer flashes for a single frame in the browser. It now shows from the first paint, keeps its phase across screens (reduced motion included) and fades out.

Rooms and categories in busy channels no longer flicker (renamed, regrouped, closed or vanishing for a few seconds) when someone joins. A late member re-announcing an older copy of a room can no longer override the newer state on screen.
Deleting a category now sticks in the sidebar. Re-announcements from before the deletion no longer bring it back.
Messages from a previous epoch are attributed using that epoch's tree. Before, a message from someone who had just been removed or re-seated could be dropped, or credited to whoever took their leaf.
When someone joins a channel, members without a role no longer repeat the room list while the channel's admin is still announcing it. One join now sends the rooms once instead of several times.
Server: the common-room join card is accepted up to 8 MiB (it was capped at 256 KiB, about 68 members). Large common rooms accept self-service joins again.

Reduced motion no longer makes the voice halo jump between levels: it still moves in 10% steps, but each step now glides at half speed (180 ms) instead of snapping. Same for the green ring. The universal reduced-motion rule zeroed these transitions; the halo rules now override it.
SFU calls: people re-seated in the channel (new MLS leaf) stayed silent for the rest of the session while shown as connected. Media keys are now looked up by the person's current leaf.

SFU calls: a stream whose media key arrives late waits paused instead of showing as connected while silent. It opens on the next epoch change; until then the call shows "no sound yet" with notice 447.
Sign-up now asks whether to join the Orwell channel (checked by default). You can join later from Communities > "Join the Orwell channel".
Windows installer no longer asks "all users or just me". It always installs per-user and still lets you pick the folder.
Windows: per-machine installs ("all users") receive updates again. Windows asks for permission once.
Leaving the Orwell channel no longer re-joins you on next launch.
Checkbox tick is centered again on Windows.
Remember session: a checkbox on login lets Orwell open next time without asking for your password. On by default. Toggle it in Settings > Account > Session; "Log out" clears it.
Account switching: Settings > Account > Session > "Switch account" keeps the current account on this device and opens another. Each account has its own vault and session.
Desktop: new splash screen and installer.
Desktop: accounts without a password can now set one in Settings > Account > Session. New accounts always get a password.
YouTube embeds in community rooms: thumbnails are now cached, and one room no longer wipes the thumbnails of other rooms.
Desktop: "Log out" on a passwordless account no longer reopens it automatically.
A device removed from a passwordless account no longer prompts for a password that doesn't exist; it shows "Start over" instead.
Desktop: "Switch account", "Delete account" and "Merge accounts" reload the app when done again.
Mic sensitivity: set the threshold below which your mic doesn't transmit, with a live meter. Settings > Voice.
Moderation: "Move to" with nested rooms, and "Disconnect from call". The founder can rename the admin role.
Friend activity alerts: when a friend joins a voice room, starts screen sharing or joins one of your channels. Each alert has its own toggle in Settings > Notifications.
Missed calls: an unanswered private call now shows up in notifications.
When a friend comes online, a toast with their avatar and an "Open chat" button appears in the corner. Auto-dismisses after 2 s.
Notifications open in a window, grouped by day, with All, Mentions, Calls, Invites and Friends filters.
Joining a channel now shows its name, rooms, roles and members right away, even if nobody is online.
Bigger calls: up to 50 people, 4 cameras and 2 screen shares at once.
Near-zero bandwidth when nobody is talking. Voice quality unchanged.
Broken screen share or camera video now recovers in under a second.
When the server is at capacity, new streams get Error 446. Calls already in progress are unaffected.
Game overlay is now off by default (enable it in Settings). Notifications are on by default and sounds at 100%.
Users with the "move" permission can move people without asking them first.
Desktop: notifications no longer show as "blocked by the browser".
Channel names show up again after a page reload.

nota: If you signed up today and don't see the Orwell channel, reload the page. Your account will join automatically.

itens.texto: Screen share at 30 FPS (up from 15).
Since the morning of Nov 2, new accounts couldn't join the Orwell channel. Fixed.

nota: Windows desktop app auto-updates from this version on. If you're on 1.0.6, install 1.0.7 manually one last time.

itens.texto: Desktop game overlay: who's in the room, who's talking and who joins, on top of your game. Drag it wherever you want.
AFK room: muted users in a voice room are moved there automatically, and come back with one click.
Audio sharing: a browser tab, system audio or a window, on top of files.
Fullscreen screen share: corner button or double-click. Esc exits.
Windows desktop app now auto-updates on launch, only to builds we signed.
Per-user call volume: 0 to 200% slider in the user menu.
YouTube thumbnails open the video in a new window, outside the app.
Screen share audio is always included, no checkbox.
Friend online toast auto-dismisses after 2 s.
Voice is prioritized over video on poor connections.
Joining a community with no admin online could leave you without the room list.
Mobile: room list closed when tapping a community whose rooms were still loading.
Browser: viewers of a screen share had no audio until they clicked a button.
Paired device: a new private chat stayed under Communities until the primary device came online.
Safari paired device showed Error 349 and recreated the account wall. The error message no longer exposes the channel address.
Desktop: external links and the outbound filter now check the full URL.

nota: Camera and screen share from 1.0.6 aren't visible on 1.0.5. Please update.

itens.texto: New devices receive history: chats, walls, tickets and files.
Crop your profile picture, channel icon and cover before saving.
Alert when a friend comes online, with their avatar and name.
Short sounds on mute/unmute and deafen.
"LIVE" badge on screen shares, with viewer count.
Desktop: global hotkeys that work while minimized. Any key or mouse buttons 4 and 5.
Messages a device missed while offline are synced, encrypted, from another device on the account.
Ringtone only plays for private messages.
System notifications also show with the window focused, except for the open chat.
Other people's audio dropped when someone joined or left a call.
Screen share showed a partial image.
Two devices on the same account in the same call were using the same keys.
Profiles sync across devices: names show up right away on a new device.
Name changes propagate to all your devices.
Release notes in the "announcements" room of the Orwell channel.
Desktop: sign-up failed with Error 201.
Desktop: "Copy" buttons didn't copy (invites, address, "Add device").
DJ card with track, mute button and volume.
Control panel moved to the bottom of the left column, with bigger buttons.
Clearer wording in Settings.
Rewritten "How Orwell works".
Tickets now show a single warning line.
False error about read receipts.

nota: End of beta. Beta accounts don't carry over to 1.0: create a new account.

itens.texto: The server no longer knows who talks to whom: conversation addresses are encrypted.
"Merge with another account" in Devices.
Wall visible only to friends and people who share a channel with you.
Short invite and friend links: orwell.pt/c#... and orwell.pt/a#...
Invites show the channel name. The server can't see it.
Pairing only deletes the account from this device at the end, and only if everything succeeded.
With "reduced motion" on, animations stopped. They now run slower instead.
End-to-end encryption for chats, channels and calls.
Channels with rooms, roles and tickets. A wall per account.
One account across multiple devices, plus the desktop app.
